reviewer: Claude coordinator and independent Claude review agents (text, illustrations)
text: Independent review agent read the full text against Ryder's Flop-Ear and Dusty (Book IV); the frame (the monkey telling the crocodile) is stated correctly and omitted with disclosure.
The marriage lure is a non-sexual comic promise; the passionate wording and the she-donkey's suicide threats are softened for self-harm safety and disclosed.
The laundryman becomes ಯಜಮಾನ, avoiding a caste-trade label; all verses are omitted.

Age band 12+: an innocent, starving donkey is killed in one calm sentence; the jackal eating the ears and heart and talking his way out is kept, and the content note says the jackal goes unpunished. No em dashes.
illustrations: Storyboard 1024x1536, under 650 KB; seams measured at x=512 and y=512/1024; no text. One generation, no edits.
The lion, jackal and thin grey donkey are consistent and in proportion; no people. In panel 3 the lion sails over the donkey without touching it.
The donkey does not appear in panels 5 and 6; no body, meat, bones or blood anywhere. The jackal's licked lips in panel 5 only hint at the eating.
limitations: AI-agent editorial review, not human Kannada-teacher or scholar certification.
Age bands are editorial judgements against the README table and have not been tested with children, parents or adult readers.
Source fidelity was checked against saved copies of the Wikisource pages of Ryder's 1925 translation, not against Durgasimha's Kannada text or a Sanskrit recension.
Art was generated with Codex CLI on gpt-5.6-sol and judged on the full sheet and 512px panel crops with the grid measured in pixels, not in the app in dark mode.
